recommendation: Keep the audit commit. If generated publish artifacts differ during a future build, regenerate them from the terminology source rather than editing publish/ or the unrelated fhir.ini language list.
issue_request: FHIR-12756 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution to add Punjabi, Hindi, and Arabic to the Common Languages value set because the prior language list was too western-centric.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN revision 11196, preserved as git commit 3d7b361b57ba773731106768bc07aadfcfc1e0a4, which added ar/Arabic, hi/Hindi, and pa/Punjabi to source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml after revision 11195 created that ValueSet source.
additional_context: Current source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml is the authoritative terminology source and includes the requested concepts under urn:ietf:bcp:47. The checked-in publish/valueset-languages.* files are generated/stale and were not treated as source evidence. Related language-value-set issues FHIR-12451, FHIR-7959, and FHIR-8351 helped confirm the source lineage and code-system context but were not independently decided.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source change was made because the current source already satisfies the approved Jira resolution.

related_jiras.note: Revision 11195 created the Common Languages ValueSet source immediately before FHIR-12756 extended it. Current source also contains French, but this reconciliation did not need to decide FHIR-12451.
Earlier Published issue requiring ValueSet/languages to use urn:ietf:bcp:47, which the current source does.
Earlier Published issue about IETF language tag consistency for Common Languages; current source remains aligned.
